title: Molecular-communication laboratory and experimental testbed
summary: Creation of a laboratory and an operational experimental platform combining chemistry, microfluidics, instrumentation, electronics, signal processing and machine learning to validate molecular-communication theories.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: R&D Project Manager / Postdoctoral Research Associate

facts.label: Team
facts.value: Average team of five people and nine people trained in total

paragraphs: The project was conducted at King’s College London to create a molecular-communication laboratory from scratch and develop an experimental platform capable of testing theoretical models against real systems.
The testbed combined chemistry, microfluidics, UV-Visible detection, instrumentation, electronics, software and signal processing.
The experiments notably investigated the use of chemical reactions to perform filtering, saturation, amplification and encoding functions.
I identified and prepared the premises, selected and ordered equipment, fume hoods, major instruments and consumables, and contributed to defining the safety and operating protocols.
I led an average team of five people comprising a junior postdoctoral researcher, two doctoral researchers and two Master’s interns. Nine people were trained in total.
I managed two EPSRC grants of €300,000 and €60,000, contributed partially to the first proposal and wrote the second proposal in full.
I also developed the software and machine-learning tools associated with the platform, as well as the syringe pumps used in the experimental system.

features.title: Laboratory creation
features.description: Preparation of the premises, selection of equipment and definition of the protocols required to operate the laboratory.

features.title: Experimental testbed
features.description: Design of an operational platform combining chemistry, microfluidics, UV-Visible detection, electronics and software.

features.title: Chemical signal processing
features.description: Experimental investigation of filtering, saturation, amplification and encoding functions based on chemical reactions.

features.title: One-dimensional CNN analysis
features.description: Development of a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to estimate the molecular composition and concentrations of aqueous solutions from UV-Visible signals.

features.title: Open-source syringe pumps
features.description: Design and manufacture of six pumps using Fusion 360, 3D printing, Arduino electronics, I²C communication and control software.

features.title: Leadership and funding
features.description: Coordination of the team, training of users and management of two EPSRC grants representing €360,000 in total.

results: Creation of a molecular-communication laboratory from scratch.
Commissioning of an experimental testbed combining chemistry, microfluidics, instrumentation, electronics and software.
Design and manufacture of six open-source syringe pumps integrated into the platform.
Publication of “Real-time signal processing via chemical reactions for a microfluidic molecular communication system” in Nature Communications in 2023, as first author and lead writer.
Publication of “CNN-Based Detection of Mixed-Molecule Concentrations in Molecular Communication” in IEEE T-MBMC in 2026, as first author and lead writer.
